claims.text: The argument for open source security has always been Raymond's: given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow; the argument against is that the eyeballs were not there.
claims.quote: Given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow.

claims.text: In Tidelift's 2024 survey the portion of maintainers who are unpaid hobbyists remains at 60 percent.
claims.quote: The portion of respondents who reported they are unpaid hobbyists remains at 60 percent

value.unit: percent of maintainers who are unpaid hobbyists

claims.text: Proprietary software had budget for security teams and the cover of code nobody outside could read, and a lot of it got away with things that would not have survived being public.
claims.quote: It also had cover: code nobody outside could read, fewer attackers looking, products hidden behind other environments.

claims.text: Open source had efficiency: when a serious bug is reported publicly the fix rarely stops at one bug, the variations get hunted down too.
claims.quote: the fix rarely stops at the one bug: the variations get hunted down too

claims.text: The owner now runs security reviews with models on the products he works on; what took a specialist weeks takes an afternoon and can run again on the next change.
claims.quote: That used to take a specialist weeks. It now takes an afternoon, and it can run again on the next change.

claims.text: The thing open source lacked was paid attention, and that is the thing that just became abundant; being hidden is worth less every month.
claims.quote: The thing open source lacked was paid attention, and that is the thing that just became abundant.

claims.text: Anthropic's Project Glasswing update in May reported scanning more than 1,000 open-source projects and estimated 6,202 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities among the findings.
claims.quote: 6,202 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities

claims.text: Chainguard's Athena coalition reported 2,000 patches across 500 projects at its launch in June, and its harness has validated over 680 findings in over 65 projects.
claims.quote: 2,000 patches across 500 projects

claims.text: In DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge final in 2025 the systems discovered 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities and also found 18 real ones.
claims.quote: the systems "discovered 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities" and also found "18 real, non-synthetic vulnerabilities"

claims.text: The owner thought Chainguard had published the projects where its AI found nothing, with curl among them, and could not find it from Chainguard or anyone else.
claims.quote: I could not find it, from Chainguard or anyone else.

claims.text: curl ended its bug bounty on 31 January 2026; over its life it found 87 confirmed vulnerabilities, but by 2025 not even one in twenty reports was real.
claims.quote: Over its life it had found "87 confirmed vulnerabilities", but by 2025 "Not even one in twenty was real."

value.unit: confirmed vulnerabilities over the bounty's life

claims.text: In the autumn of 2025 AI-assisted reports started landing real bugs, and by May Stenberg counted that earlier tools had triggered between two and three hundred bugfixes.
claims.quote: triggered somewhere between two and three hundred bugfixes

claims.text: In May a frontier model's scan of curl found one vulnerability, of low severity, and reported zero memory-safety vulnerabilities.
claims.quote: a frontier model's scan of curl found one vulnerability, "yes, as in singular one", of low severity

claims.text: Today an AI-tooled audit produced no less than thirty-five published curl vulnerabilities, Anthropic found a high-severity bug with its OSS Scanner, and curl 8.23.0 shipped 24 security fixes.
claims.quote: no less than thirty-five published curl vulnerabilities

value.unit: curl vulnerabilities published from one audit

claims.text: That is not a project failing; it is a project getting harder to break, wave by wave, with each better tool finding what the last could not.
claims.quote: It is a project getting harder to break, wave by wave, with each better tool finding what the last one could not

claims.text: The maintainers' time is now the bottleneck, so curl's contribution rules require anyone who used an AI tool to find problems to reveal it in the report.
claims.quote: If you asked an AI tool to find problems in curl, you must make sure to reveal this fact in your report.

claims.text: The bar will rise everywhere: more findings with more proof, contributions held to a higher standard, and fewer, better projects as the long tail of tiny packages shrinks.
claims.quote: So I expect the bar to rise everywhere.

claims.text: Provenance will matter more: where a piece of code came from, who wrote it, who reviewed it.
claims.quote: And provenance will matter more: where a piece of code came from, who wrote it, who reviewed it.

claims.text: In Wardley's terms mission-critical code should be industrialised, not written at explorer speed; town planners are the people who take something and industrialise it.
claims.quote: Town Planners are brilliant people. They are able to take something and industrialise it

claims.text: You cannot have sovereignty without open source and open schemas, because you can only move what you can read and run elsewhere.
claims.quote: You cannot have sovereignty without open source and open schemas.

claims.text: The business model the owner already runs: the customer gets a private repository with their deployment, their configuration and only the features they use, and pays for it to be maintained.
claims.quote: the customer gets a private repository with their deployment, their configuration and only the features they actually use, and pays for it to be maintained

claims.text: The customer, the maintainer and security all end up aligned on running the least amount of code in production.
claims.quote: Everyone ends up aligned on running the least amount of code in production

claims.text: In The minimum code below, removing what a use case never runs took one real tool from 1,500 files to 428.
claims.quote: took one real tool from 1,500 files to 428

claims.text: For the first time the incentives of those who write, sell and secure open source point the same way: secure because the eyeballs got cheap, required for sovereignty, paid for as maintenance.
claims.quote: That is the intersection I think we are at

claims.text: There is no list of clean projects; curl's story is the evidence instead.
claims.quote: No list of clean projects.

claims.text: curl is not clean: it is a well-run project being found harder to break and still having bugs found, as of today.
claims.quote: It is a well-run project being found harder to break, and still having bugs found, as of today.

claims.text: The counts are the reporters' own: Anthropic's, Chainguard's and DARPA's figures are as they published them.
claims.quote: The counts are the reporters' own.

claims.text: The cost and depth of model review are the owner's experience on the products he works on; others will see different results.
claims.quote: The cost and depth of model review are my experience.

claims.text: The future part is an argument: fewer and better projects, a shrinking long tail and maintenance as the business are predictions.
claims.quote: The future part is an argument.
